subject: Request: time-sliced reserved GPU window and queue-priority carveout for nightly batch
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@mistralcloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@mistralcloud.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated window request — nightly batch spikes (time-slice carveout)

Marcus / Lauren,

Quick note from our infra team: over the last month we observed a recurring nightly batch across our inference workloads that spikes concurrency and tokens between 22:00–02:00 UTC. For production reliability we need a firm commitment that a portion of our reserved GPUs (equivalent to 6x A100 80GB) can run with "time-sliced" priority during that window without being queued behind multi-tenant bursts.

What we need to understand from Redwood:
- Can you offer a time-bounded queue-priority carveout (22:00–02:00 UTC) where our jobs are routed to a reserved slice with soft preemption only for critical infra events?
- How will this be reflected in the Dedicated Capacity SLA (throughput guarantees, headroom, and queueing behavior)?
- Pricing/credits for this window and any operational constraints (e.g., whether nightly jobs must be batched to a certain concurrency threshold).

I attached our sample telemetry (mistral_proposed_window_metrics.csv) to show the shape of the spike. We want to close this before Q3 launch; can we get a proposal and term sheet? Also happy to set a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sarah
VP Infrastructure — MistralCloud

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@mistralcloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated window request — nightly batch spikes (time-slice carveout)

Sarah —

Thanks for the telemetry and the clear ask. We can support a temporal carveout but there are a few tradeoffs to document, and we want to propose a pragmatic operational guardrail set so both sides have predictable behavior. High level: yes — a time-sliced priority lane (22:00–02:00 UTC) mapped to a reserved GPU subset is feasible. Key points to confirm:

1) Scope: carveout will map to your reserved pool (6 GPUs as you requested). During the window those GPUs will be routed with queue-priority for jobs tagged with your tenancy ID.

2) Preemption semantics: we propose "soft preemption" — non-zero chance of preemption only for safety events (hardware failures, urgent maintenance). We cannot offer absolute zero-preemption; we do, however, guarantee throughput headroom of ~95% of steady-state capacity during the carveout window as an SLA guarantee.

3) Canary & telemetry: we recommend a 6-week canary (2 weeks low-traffic, 4 weeks production-shaped load) with enhanced tracing and automatic rollback criteria. During canary, we will monitor token-level latency P50/P95 and queue depth.

4) Pricing: we can offer a temporary 20% usage credit covering the first 30 days of the carveout window, then standard reserved pricing. The formal term sheet is attached (redwood_time_slice_term_sheet_v1.pdf).

5) Edge cases: if your nightly workloads exceed the reserved slice consistently (beyond agreed burst threshold), we will: a) trigger an autoscaling/overflow routing to a lower-cost burst pool, and b) log quota events for remediation. We'll need to agree on a daily peak threshold to avoid surprises.

I attached an initial term sheet with the above language. Lauren / Ben — can you review the proposed preemption wording and SLA numbers? If we're aligned, I'll prepare an amendment for signatures and a JIRA ticket for onboarding.

Marcus Lin
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
(mobile: +1 415 555 0192)

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@mistralcloud.com>

Cc: contracts@mistralcloud.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated window request — nightly batch spikes (time-slice carveout)

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:

• The 6 GPUs are baseline; we do burst to an additional 2–4 GPUs during the window when nightly dedup runs kick in. We can cap burst at +4 and signal via tenancy tag.
• For the canary, we want the first two weeks to be shadow (no impact to production) and then the 4-week production-shaped run.
• The telemetry we attached includes token-distribution per-job and a rough breakdown of short-lived vs long-lived sessions — happy to walk the team through it on a brief call.

Also, can you confirm if the 20% credit applies retroactively to the first day of the window activation or only from the day we sign the amendment? We prefer retroactive to activation. Finally, can you add a clause that guarantees a max P95 latency increase of +50ms vs baseline during the carveout (we understand this is measured at token-level and within reason).

If this is acceptable we'll route to our procurement for a redline. Please include a sample DocuSign link when you have the amendment.

Best,
Sarah
VP Infrastructure — MistralCloud

Subject: Re: Dedicated window request — nightly batch spikes (time-slice carveout)

Sarah / Marcus —

Quick follow-up from ops/offerings: we can accept the burst cap (+4 GPUs) and retroactive credit to activation date. We'll add the P95 latency protection as a measurable objective in the SLA addendum but need to be explicit about measurement (token-level P95 measured by Redwood's observability pipeline, excluding noisy network-level anomalies and scheduled maintenance windows). Proposed next steps: 

1) I will update the term sheet to reflect: burst cap +4, retroactive 20% credit to activation, and a P95 token-latency objective (+50ms tolerance) with defined exclusion windows.
2) We'll attach a 6-week canary plan as an exhibit (shadow 2 weeks -> 4 weeks production-shaped).
3) Ben will open the onboarding JIRA (RWI-3258) and I'll create the DocuSign envelope.

Ben — please confirm you have capacity to run the canary and set the tracing flags for tenancy sampling. Sarah — expect a redline-ready amendment by EOD tomorrow; after procurement sign-off we can schedule onboarding (typical lead time: 7 business days for reserved-pool mapping).

Lauren Bishop
Head of Offerings, Redwood Inference
